title: dfn panel for https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#comment-state is 12.2.5.45 “Comment state” is broken due to a hardcoded ID conflicting with generated ID
body:
Go to https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#comment-state and click on the **12.2.5.45 Comment state** heading and you’ll get a popup dfn panel that has **#comment** as the anchor and **No references in this specification**. There are in fact references in the spec to *comment state* — but those are to the `comment-state` ID, not the `comment` ID. The cause is that the source looks like this: ```html
12.2.5.45 Comment state
``` That is, there are two IDs: the `h5` heading element itself has a `comment-state` ID, and its child `dfn` has a `comment` ID. The `comment` ID is hardcoded into the `dfn` element in the markup source. I think that’s the ultimate cause of the problem. So I think the fix is, we start by removing the hardcoded `comment` ID from the `dfn`. Then we have two options: 1. Preserve the existing `comment` ID (and so not end up changing the target of any external links to it that might exist).
To do that, we can move the explicit `comment` ID to the `h5` element.
If we did that, then all of the internal references to *comment state* would continue to link back to the `comment` ID (and the dfn panel will work as expected). 2. Don’t preserve the exisiting `comment` ID.
To do that, we just don’t add the `comment` ID to the `h5` element (after dropping it from the `dfn` element).
If we did that, then all of the internal references to *comment state* would now link back to the `comment-state` ID (and the dfn panel will work as expected). I don’t feel strongly about it either way — but looking back at the revision history shows that the hardcoded `comment` ID has been in the source since the first time it was checked into revision control, in 2006 — and there are no internal references to that `comment` ID anywhere in the current source. So I think that suggests we could safely drop the `comment` ID completely (option 2 above).
